title: Routing change sends traffic to a slice that was already worse
tell: The fleet error rate rises while no individual slice's error rate changes. Decomposition puts the whole move in the mix term and leaves the rate term near zero.
The implicated slice was already elevated in the baseline window, often for long enough that nobody considered it an incident.
Fleet-wide traffic is flat, because a redistribution moves requests between slices without changing the total. Only the per-slice shares move.
This pages whoever owns routing or load balancing, not the service owner. Nothing in the serving path got worse.

confusable_with.discriminator: A degradation shows a rate effect: the slice's own error rate is higher than it was in the baseline. Here the slice's rate is unchanged and only its share of traffic grew.

If the receiving slice is failing because the extra traffic overwhelmed it, its error rate will also have risen, giving a rate effect alongside the mix effect. A pure mix effect means it is failing at exactly the rate it always did.
